statement: For all positive real r,q,t satisfying r+q-2 >= sqrt(5)|r-q| and t^2 >= (1+2r+2q)/5, the supremum of P(r,q,t)^alpha=(q/t^2)^(5/4) is ((5+sqrt(5))/4)^(5/4). No finite feasible triple attains the supremum. For every integer n>=1, q_n=n, r_n=((sqrt(5)-1)+(3-sqrt(5))n)/2, and t_n=sqrt((sqrt(5)+(5-sqrt(5))n)/5) form a feasible exact sequence whose objective values converge to that supremum. The scope is only the frozen displayed three-parameter family and asserts nothing about equality with the global constant f(alpha).
contribution: This completely resolves the frozen family optimization by proving the exact sharp constant, strict nonattainment, and an exact extremal sequence, while independently recovering the published feasibility characterization. The cited primary paper gives the characterization and one value above 2 but does not state this sharp family result; no broader priority claim is made.
